newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds finish lower, follow U.S. bonds.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds finish lower, follow U.S. bonds.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished lower Monday, as the market slipped with U.S. Treasuries in slim trade.
"The market is just playing against Treasuries," said a trader at a local bank. "There was very little volume."
The 30-year U.S. Treasury yields was last up four basis points at 6.70 percent.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was down 3/8 at 93-7/8 while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 was down $0.17 at 121.00.
Traders added that the market remained underpinned despite its high levels.
"The market is sustained but expensive," said another trader.
Market players predicted the market would continue being led by U.S. Treasuries this week. The release of U.S. consumer confidence figures for the month of June Tuesday will also be watched closely.
"If the consumer confidence figures are good more gains are likely," added the trader.
Call money rose to 5.7 percent from 5.6 percent.
